import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, LogisticRegression
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.metrics import (
    mean_squared_error,
    mean_absolute_error,
    r2_score,
    accuracy_score,
    confusion_matrix,
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay,
    classification_report,
    roc_curve,
    roc_auc_score
)

plt.rcParams["figure.figsize"] = (7,5)

In [52]:
X = housing[['Avg. Area Income',
             'Avg. Area House Age',
             'Avg. Area Number of Rooms',
             'Avg. Area Number of Bedrooms',
             'Area Population']]

y = housing['Price']

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.4, random_state=101
)

linear_model = LinearRegression()
linear_model.fit(X_train, y_train)

)

Feature Scaling¶

In [27]:
scaler = StandardScaler()

X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)

X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)

Training the model¶

Conclusion¶

  • Implemented Multiple Linear Regression using the USA Housing dataset.
  • Predicted house prices using five numerical features.
  • Evaluated the model using MAE, MSE, RMSE and R² Score.
  • Performed Residual Analysis and 5-fold Cross Validation for robust validation.
  • Implemented Binary Logistic Regression using the Diabetes dataset.
  • Applied Feature Scaling before model training.
  • Evaluated performance using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Confusion Matrix and ROC-AUC.
  • The experiment demonstrates the practical application of supervised learning for both regression and classification tasks.
